unjudged.title: Successful agent runs can be reported as failures due to unconditional post-exit kill
unjudged.evidence: The process group is killed in the finally block for every run, then the code checks 'if proc.returncode != 0' without refreshing the return code after that kill. A fast command can finish, be SIGKILLed in the finally block before 'proc.returncode' is set, and then be treated as a non-zero exit.
unjudged.recommendation: Only kill the process group on timeout/error, or first wait for the child to exit and capture its return code before any cleanup kill of background descendants. If you need to reap stray children after normal completion, avoid sending SIGKILL to the main process once it has exited.
